title: Teaching the Message of the Restoration (Part 1)
intro: This lesson prepares learners to teach the first part of the message of the Restoration: God is our loving Father, families matter to Him, He leads His children through prophets, and the gospel was lost in the Great Apostasy. By the end, each learner can teach these truths simply and testify.
preparation: Study Amos 8:11–12, Isaiah 24:5, 2 Thessalonians 2:3, Acts 20:29–30, 2 Timothy 4:3–4 and Ephesians 4:11–14. Read “The Family: A Proclamation to the World” and bring a copy for each learner. Pray for each learner by name.

steps.why: Teach the idea and why it matters for a missionary.

examples.title: Define the key words
examples.text: Write three words on the board: apostasy, dispensation and prophet. Ask learners to say each one in their own words. Then give the plain meaning. Apostasy is turning away from the truth. A dispensation is a time when God has a prophet on the earth with priesthood keys. A prophet is a man God calls to speak for Him.

examples.title: Draw the pattern
examples.text: Draw a circle of four steps: God calls a prophet, the gospel is taught, people turn away, God calls a prophet again. Explain that earlier dispensations ended in apostasy, and that God restored the gospel again through prophets. Read Amos 3:7 to show that God leads His children through prophets.

examples.title: Ask the key question
examples.text: Write on the board: What led to the Great Apostasy, and what came of it? Let learners search for answers in Amos 8:11–12 and Acts 20:29–30. Then sum up. After Jesus Christ and His Apostles died, changes that no one had authority to make crept into doctrine and practice. In time, priesthood keys and authority were taken from the earth.

steps.why: Show one example of what learners will do.

examples.title: Teach one learner
examples.text: Teach one learner who has never heard of the Apostasy. Keep it to three minutes: one idea, one scripture, one question. Let the class see how you listen and how you answer.

examples.title: Explain two scriptures
examples.text: Read Amos 8:11–12 and Acts 20:29–30 aloud. Show how to explain each in one sentence. Then say what it means for the person you are teaching.

examples.title: Use a three-part outline
examples.text: Write on the board: 1. God has always led His children through prophets. 2. After the Apostles died, truth and authority were lost. 3. God restored the gospel through a prophet. Teach from the outline.

steps.why: Learners practise in pairs or small groups.

examples.title: Teach in pairs
examples.text: Form pairs. Each pair prepares a four to five minute lesson on the Apostasy with one or two scriptures. It should be simple, clear and fitted to the listener. Then each pair teaches another pair.

examples.title: Study, then share
examples.text: Learners study 2 Thessalonians 2:3, Isaiah 24:5 and 2 Timothy 4:3–4 on their own. They look for what the prophets said would happen to Christ’s Church. Each shares what they found with a partner. Write this summary: ancient prophets foretold a falling away from the truth.

examples.title: Role play in threes
examples.text: Make groups of three: a missionary, a friend and an evaluator. The friend asks, “Why did the gospel need to be restored?” The missionary answers. The evaluator gives feedback. Rotate the roles.

steps.why: Name what went well and what can improve.

examples.title: Partner feedback
examples.text: The learner who was taught says what was most meaningful. Each teacher writes one thing to keep and one thing to improve.

examples.title: Three questions
examples.text: Ask: What went well? What could you do better? What helped most in explaining what happened after the Apostles died? Begin with the good and encourage every learner.

examples.title: Simple checklist
examples.text: Ask: Was it simple? Was it clear? Was a scripture used and explained? Did it fit the listener? Did the teacher testify?

steps.why: Practise again with what was learned.

examples.title: Switch roles
examples.text: The pair that was taught now teaches. Leave time for feedback both ways. Then invite a few learners to share what they learned.

examples.title: Improve one thing
examples.text: Each learner teaches again and changes one thing from the feedback: a clearer sentence, a better scripture or a simpler question.

examples.title: Teach a new partner
examples.text: Find a new partner. Teach the same lesson in three minutes. Then share one insight with the whole class.

testimony: Invite learners to share their testimony that God restored His gospel through a prophet.

tips.text: Open with prayer and a short thought from scripture to invite the Holy Ghost.
Ask questions that need more than a yes or no.
Let learners find truths in the scriptures first, then explain them in their own words.
Start with a real-life situation and ask what the learner would do.

quote.text: If you will listen to the living prophet and the apostles and heed our counsel, you will not go astray.
quote.by: Elder M. Russell Ballard, “His Word Ye Shall Receive,” April 2001 general conference

study: Study Doctrine and Covenants 1:37–38 together and ask what it teaches about the words of God’s servants.
invitations: Study the Topical Guide entry on the Apostasy of the early Christian church. Write in your study journal the scriptures you could use to teach it.
Teach the Great Apostasy in four minutes to a family member or friend this week.
Begin to memorize Joseph Smith’s own account of the First Vision, Joseph Smith—History 1:17, to prepare for the next class.

sections.title: God is our loving Father
paras: Begin with a case study. A friend writes late at night, discouraged, and asks: “Is God real? Does He care about us? What is He like?” Let a few learners say how they would answer. Then explain that today’s lesson prepares them to answer.

Search scripture together for how God shows His love, for example Romans 8:16 and Moses 1:39. Ask learners to write a short statement: God is our loving Father and wants all of His children to return to Him. Ask why a person should understand this before learning other doctrines.

sections.title: The gospel blesses families
paras: Let learners read “The Family: A Proclamation to the World” and mark the phrases that show the role of marriage and family in God’s plan. Ask a learner to write them on the board.

Read this from President Boyd K. Packer, “The Father and the Family,” general conference, April 1994: “The ultimate purpose of the adversary … is to disrupt, disturb, and destroy the home and the family” (see Revelation 12:12). Ask why the family is such a target, and how the proclamation helps a missionary tell God’s plan from the world’s trends. Keep the focus on God’s plan, and do not spend long on worldly trends.

sections.title: Prophets and dispensations
paras: Explain that calling prophets is one way God shows His love. Read what Elder M. Russell Ballard taught in “His Word Ye Shall Receive,” general conference, April 2001: “If you will listen to the living prophet and the apostles and heed our counsel, you will not go astray.” Read Doctrine and Covenants 1:37–38, Amos 3:7 and 1 Nephi 3:7. Ask what blessings come to those who follow the Lord’s prophet.

Teach the pattern: God calls a prophet, the gospel is taught, people turn away, and God calls a prophet again. A time when God has a prophet with priesthood keys is called a dispensation. Ask why it helps an investigator to know that earlier dispensations ended in apostasy.

sections.title: The Savior’s earthly ministry
paras: Ask what Jesus Christ did to establish His Church. He chose and ordained Apostles and gave them authority. His ministry and rejection followed the pattern of earlier dispensations. After the deaths of the Savior and His Apostles, people fell into apostasy again until God called a prophet to restore the gospel.

sections.title: The Great Apostasy
paras: Write this question on the board: What led to the Great Apostasy, and what came of it? Let learners search for answers. After the deaths of Jesus Christ and His Apostles, changes that no one had authority to make crept into doctrine and practice. In time, priesthood keys and authority were taken from the earth.

Let learners study some of the verses about the falling away, such as 2 Thessalonians 2:3, Amos 8:11–12 and 2 Timothy 4:3–4. Write this summary: ancient prophets foretold a falling away from the truth. Then move to the training steps, where learners teach the Apostasy in pairs.

blocks.text: Welcome the class warmly. Begin with a prayer and a short thought from scripture to invite the Holy Ghost.
What happened when you tried last lesson’s invitation? Who would like to share?
Listen for: real experiences, effort made, one thing learned.
Try saying: “Before we start, who would like to tell us what happened when they tried last week’s invitation?”
Keep the review short. Let two or three learners share, and thank each one.

blocks.title: The Family: A Proclamation to the World, key lines
blocks.text: The proclamation is one page that states what God has revealed about the family. Three lines learners can mark: “The family is ordained of God.” Marriage between a man and a woman is essential to His eternal plan. And happiness in family life is most likely when it is founded upon the teachings of the Lord Jesus Christ. It also says that parents have a sacred duty to rear their children in love and righteousness, to provide for their needs, and to teach them to love and serve one another. Have each learner read their own copy and mark what stands out.
Let learners read “The Family: A Proclamation to the World” and mark the phrases that show the role of marriage and family in God’s plan.
Ask a learner to write them on the board.

Read this from President Boyd K. Packer, “The Father and the Family,” general conference, April 1994: “The ultimate purpose of the adversary … is to disrupt, disturb, and destroy the home and the family” (see Revelation 12:12).
Ask why the family is such a target, and how the proclamation helps a missionary tell God’s plan from the world’s trends.
Keep the focus on God’s plan, and do not spend long on worldly trends.
Listen for: marriage and families are ordained of God and central to His plan.
Show the Proclamation. Say: “God’s plan places families at the center.”
Let learners mark phrases before they speak.
Explain that calling prophets is one way God shows His love.

Listen for: prophets show God’s love; those who follow them are blessed.
Say: “God has always led His children through living prophets.”
Write the cycle on the board: prophet, gospel, turning away, prophet again.

Listen for: ordination, keys and authority.
Say: “Jesus Christ chose Apostles and gave them authority.”
Ask what authority means to learners.
